words: Comparable entries are needed to separate timing from the exits that follow.
context: Comparable entries are needed to separate timing from the exits that follow. Each line entry got twenty random twins, later times drawn with repeats from the next sixty trading days. Each twin shared the entry's fund, direction and time of day, in similar prior market conditions. Each twin copied the line's slope, clearance and initial stop distance for its exits. That copy was a constructed reference, not a line found at the random time. Matching still left unequal exposure to recent price swings, and we cannot tell which way that tilted the result. Our registered plan set five coverage gates. Six of the twenty-four found no match, leaving eighteen, below the required ninety percent. Those eighteen setups and their twins made eighteen groups, against five hundred required. Each fund needed fifty groups, and even QQQ fell short. Thirteen calendar quarters were represented, below the required twenty-four. Only the data-completeness check passed, since nearly every day's record was complete, leaving one of five coverage gates satisfied. The next hurdle is knowing how each comparison ended.
